The minimum value of the reciprocal of the product of the roots is 64.

**Setup.** Write f(x) = ∏_{i=1}^6 (x − r_i) with each r_i ∈ [0,1], where the roots are counted with multiplicity. Because the degree is even, f(0) = ∏ r_i. Also f(1) = ∏ (1 − r_i).

**Condition.** f(0) = f(1) gives P := ∏ r_i = ∏ (1 − r_i).

The reciprocal 1/P must be defined, so P > 0. (If P = 0, then some r_i = 0, so the condition forces some r_j = 1. The reciprocal would then be undefined.) Hence every r_i ∈ (0,1).

**Bound.** Multiplying the two expressions for P gives

P² = ∏ r_i(1 − r_i).

For each i, r_i(1 − r_i) ≤ 1/4 by AM–GM. So P² ≤ (1/4)^6 = 1/4096, which gives P ≤ 1/64 and hence 1/P ≥ 64.

**Attainment.** Take f(x) = (x − 1/2)^6. All roots are real and lie in (0,1), and f(0) = f(1) = 1/64. Here P = 1/64, so 1/P = 64.

Final answer: 64
